context:
Goal: a finished lane archives without a session guessing why the guard refused.
Problem (goal): you picked 937 a, where the guard reads a public repo's open PRs anonymously. The consultant measured at 14:15 CST that in a cloud session the session proxy refuses an unattached public repo even with no token (cli/cli answered 403, "GitHub access to this repository is not enabled... add_repo"). An attached repo reads anonymously fine. So the anonymous read only helps where a session has direct internet access, which today means local sessions, not the cloud where the incident happened. Only you can say whether it is still worth building.
Based on (measured): consultant, 14:15 CST Nov 17: cli/cli 403 from the proxy with no token; claude-settings (attached) returned 505 open PRs anonymously.
Based on (ruling): own-937-a (owner, 2026-11-17 13:11 CST, the guard reads a public repo's open PRs anonymously; a private repo's refusal names add_repo access push, then retry)
Departs from: ruling 937 a — the "reads anonymously" half; a keeps it, b drops it and keeps only the add_repo access push remedy text.
Meanwhile: draft PR #3136 stays at 764e0adf21; the consultant builds nothing more on it until you answer.

lastAnswer.note: b) Drop the anonymous read; keep only the add_repo access push remedy. Owner chat 14:20 CST Nov 17, relayed by the consultant: "Gotcha on 937 then just do the option that has you add in the repo you need".
